original_target.title: Positive-area images of non-removable Jordan curves
original_target.area: Complex analysis, conformal welding and geometric measure theory

full_original_statement:
Let $`\Gamma`$ be a closed Jordan curve in the Riemann sphere. Write $`CH(\Gamma)`$ for the sphere homeomorphisms that are conformal away from $`\Gamma`$. The curve is *conformally removable* if every map in $`CH(\Gamma)`$ is Möbius.

**Question.** If $`\Gamma`$ is not conformally removable, must there exist $`f\in CH(\Gamma)`$ such that $`f(\Gamma)`$ has positive planar area (after choosing a sphere chart avoiding one point of the image)?

The quantifier ranges over **every** non-removable Jordan curve. The known flexible-curve case alone does not answer it. This is Bishop's Question 7 and the curve case of Younsi's Question 5.27.
queries: site:arxiv.org OR site:zenodo.org OR site:hal.science OR site:github.com "Flexible curves" "Hausdorff"

sources.scope_comparison: Corollary1.3's positive-area CH-image conclusion is for flexible curves only, and the actual body states all non-removable curves as Conjecture1.5. Residual/generic flexible curves do not prove the universal local quantifier. Generic noninjective welding or constructing a curve fixed by a non-Möbius map does not imply positive-area image for every input curve. No all-curve announcement located.
